resolution: Settled by printed text, read literally: Pure ignores "all other attributes", and the Manual names Tough as an attribute ("4. Attributes like Tough"), so Tough, Balanced, Inverted and Unaware do not apply in a Pure interaction. The owner ruling of 2026-08-20 (“{Pure}: the attribute layer, switched off…”)’s "stats are not attributes" is our ruling and does not change what the Manual calls Tough. attr.general.pure states print; the owner followed print on 2026-10-22 and the engine was changed (CT-260; F-U19-1 closed, 555). Document fix: done 2026-10-10. attr.pure.stat-attributes (which stated the owner ruling of 2026-09-05 (“{Pure} outside combat: the same switch…”)) and attr.pure.unaware-combat (which stated the owner ruling of 2026-08-23 (“STAT LAYER 6, {Unaware}: everything in…”)) contradicted attr.general.pure; both now state print and are marked engine-differs (F-U19-1, F-U19-2). Register fix: mark the owner ruling of 2026-09-05 (“{Pure} outside combat: the same switch…”)’s "still read" sentence and the owner ruling of 2026-08-23 (“STAT LAYER 6, {Unaware}: everything in…”)’s "survives {Pure}" as outranked by the printed reminder.

summary: Whether a unit without Flying may block a Flying column together with a Flying unit in the same blocking column. The printed reminder names units; the Manual says "the blocking unit"; the Rulebook says "unless the defending player also has flying units"; the owner ruling of 2026-08-29 (“the reminder a player reads is…”) records that the client "blocks by COLUMN".

sides.quote: Only flying units can block flying units.
blocked unless the blocking unit has flying.
Flying attribute and the entire column cannot be blocked unless the defending player
blocks by COLUMN and the authored row said so.
Its column can only be blocked by a column with Flying.

resolution: Settled by the designer (2026-10-24 audit), reading A: asked whether a back unit that could not block may join a front unit that could, Caleb answered "Columns share attributes, so if any unit in the column has flying, the entire column has flying" (RQ 1348502069614612563). attr.flying.blocking now states it; the engine already checks the blocking column's attributes, pinned by 633.

summary: The owner ruling of 2026-08-23 (“STAT LAYER 6, {Unaware}: everything in…”) is unmarked although its "one open edge" paragraph (targeting is deliberately not implemented) was answered by the owner ruling of 2026-08-30 (“a document validated against the code…”); only the owner ruling of 2026-08-26 (“the glossary is a rules document…”)’s Unaware row carries the owner ruling of 2026-08-30 (“a document validated against the code…”) mark.

resolution: Follow the owner ruling of 2026-08-30 (“a document validated against the code…”): an Unaware card can be targeted, and stat changes put on it do nothing while it is Unaware. Mark the owner ruling of 2026-08-23 (“STAT LAYER 6, {Unaware}: everything in…”)’s targeting paragraph "(answered by the owner ruling of 2026-08-30 (“a document validated against the code…”))". Still open, and conditional: whether a stat-gated target restriction ("base power 2 or less") reads the printed stats of a non-Unaware target when the effect's source is Unaware. Question for the owner only if a card can put such a restriction on an Unaware source (no printed card does today: Bubb, Trashling and Haboob have no targeted text).

summary: The Tough + Inverted law rests on the owner's retracted bug report and the owner ruling of 2026-08-28 (“{Tough} + {Inverted}: the owner's own…”)’s derivation; the owner's own words ("always kills") are stronger than the law the owner ruling of 2026-08-28 (“{Tough} + {Inverted}: the owner's own…”) pins (a shrunk unit survives).

sides.quote: > works. So tough + inverted always kills the unit since +0/+X is just -0/-X
> ### **final defense = −2Δ.** The base cancels out completely.

resolution: Follow the owner ruling of 2026-08-28 (“{Tough} + {Inverted}: the owner's own…”): the rule states the law (defense = -2 x the net change), which is the owner's statement for every board where the defense has not been reduced. No designer source; Caleb's nearby remark ("tough inverted would die before you could add more", the owner ruling of 2026-08-23 (“Stat layer 5: {Inverted} negates the…”)) agrees with the common case.
